lead: Plaça de l'Oca with its craft fair, a neighbourhood cinema and plenty of community life.
text: It occupies the area formerly known as the Camp de l'Arpa and parts of the traditional Clot. Plaça de l'Oca, with its craft fair, is one of its liveliest corners, and the Cinema Foment Martinenc keeps up the cultural offer of a neighbourhood where the traditional cinema still has its place.

Although it is not a tourist neighbourhood, it has numerous schools, theatres, a youth centre and a senior citizens' centre, and the Hospital del Nen Déu. With 53,354 inhabitants/km², it is one of the densest neighbourhoods in Barcelona, and its average sale price is 4,243 €/m².
housing: Blocks of flats from different periods, on dense, well-equipped streets.
